ko.executive_summary: Qualcomm is raising Snapdragon chip prices by potentially double digits starting September 1st, driven by memory cost surges. Meanwhile, Qualcomm, MediaTek SoC shipments fell over 25% as Apple, Samsung, Google, and UNISOC gain market share; however, Qualcomm secured a long-term supply deal with BMW for digital cockpit and autonomous driving platforms through the next decade.
key_facts: Snapdragon price increase effective September 1st, potentially double digit
Qualcomm and MediaTek SoC shipments fell over 25%
GenAI chips grew 24%
Qualcomm named BMW Group's lead compute silicon provider for digital cockpit and automated driving

implications.text: Memory cost inflation cascading to end-product SoC pricing will compress OEM margins and potentially dampen smartphone upgrade cycles.
Apple, Samsung, Google, and UNISOC capturing smartphone SoC demand signals consolidation toward in-house and differentiated custom silicon strategies.
Long-term BMW supply deal diversifies Qualcomm revenue beyond mobile and toward higher-margin automotive digital/autonomous platforms.

ko.counterpoint: Snapdragon price increases may face customer resistance or demand destruction if memory prices stabilize before Q4 2024.

ko.executive_summary: SK hynix is fundamentally overhauling its hiring process to prioritize AI-era talent, replacing traditional résumés with half-day deep-dive interviews and removing academic credential barriers. NVIDIA is expanding AI R&D efforts with a new center in South Korea, while an NYSE-listed AI chip design firm made a secondary listing in Singapore.
key_facts: SK hynix scrapped traditional self-introduction essays; introduced half-day in-depth interviews
SK hynix removed academic credential barriers in new hire recruitment
SK hynix CEO Kwak No-jung stated regional investment and young talent relocation support are interconnected priorities
NVIDIA opened new R&D center in South Korea for AI efforts
NYSE-listed AI chip design firm listed secondarily in Singapore

implications.text: SK hynix's shift to competency-based, AI-native hiring reflects intensifying competition for specialized AI/ML engineering talent in HPC/datacenter supply chains.
Coupling hiring innovation with regional development support indicates strategy to grow engineering centers outside Seoul amid government incentives for fab decentralization.
South Korea R&D center expansion underscores NVIDIA's deepening partnership ecosystem and local validation of AI accelerator roadmaps in memory-adjacent supply chains.

ko.counterpoint: Structural hiring process changes may lag in execution if middle-management resistance slows adoption or if regional talent pools remain underdeveloped.

ko.executive_summary: Microsoft is scaling custom AI accelerator buildout with Maia 200 and MAI models, with CEO Nadella pitching swappable AI models for flexibility. Amazon is positioning custom chipmaking as a next major business pillar, while strong demand for custom silicon is boosting test equipment vendors; additionally, ChipAgents raised $134M as semiconductor giants adopt AI-assisted chip design.
key_facts: Microsoft Maia 200 custom AI accelerator buildout underway
Microsoft scaling MAI custom models with architecture flexibility
Amazon positioning custom chipmaking as next business pillar
ChipAgents raised $134 million for AI-assisted chip design
Broadcom expanded AR55 Absolute Encoder ASIC portfolio
Global Unichip 2Q net income surpassed estimates at NT$1.56B
Teradyne market outlook boosted by strong custom silicon demand

implications.text: Microsoft and Amazon custom silicon expansion signals strategic shift away from merchant GPU/CPU dependency; threatens traditional fabless AI chip design economics.
ChipAgents' $134M funding and adoption by semiconductor giants indicates AI-augmented chip design becoming table-stakes, compressing design cycles and time-to-market.
Custom SoCs and ASICs addressing specific workloads (motion control, inference) enable sustainable product differentiation and reduce procurement risk from single-source dependencies.

ko.counterpoint: Hyperscaler custom silicon initiatives require 2-3 year design cycles and billion-dollar fab commitments, creating execution risk and potential capex overallocation if AI demand moderates.

ko.executive_summary: Samsung foundry is aggressively pursuing 2nm design wins—reportedly doubling in 2026—backed by a secretive cloud giant customer and Broadcom negotiations, targeting profit turnaround. TSMC is advancing 1.4nm mass production targeting mid-2028 using AI to mitigate construction and thermal risks; Samsung also plans to double foundry orders in 2026. Both Samsung and TSMC are adopting advanced packaging (EMIB-like) and driving sub-8nm utilization expansion.
key_facts: Samsung 2nm design wins expected to double in 2026
Samsung foundry running sub-8nm lines at full capacity; fast-tracking Taylor, Texas plants
Samsung Broadcom partnership under negotiation for 2nm volume
TSMC 1.4nm mass production targeted mid-2028; first building expected before April 2027
TSMC implementing AI to reduce 1.4nm construction risk and thermal hazards
TSMC adopting EMIB-like packaging technology with Kinsus
Samsung DS unit delivered 99.7% of Q2 profit; HBM4 revenue forecast to triple in Q3

implications.text: Samsung and TSMC simultaneous sub-8nm expansion and advanced node ramp create binning/yield risk; market may absorb excess capacity at depressed pricing if AI demand normalizes.
Samsung's aggressive 2nm win targeting and Broadcom deal attempt signal existential threat to TSMC's AI foundry dominance, though execution risk remains high.
Both foundries adopting chiplet/EMIB-style packaging to overcome reticle limits and cost pressures, accelerating heterogeneous integration as de facto standard for next-gen AI accelerators.
Samsung's memory profitability (HBM4, DRAM/NAND) funding foundry losses; tight coupling of memory and logic roadmaps creates competitive moat but adds financial volatility.

ko.counterpoint: Samsung's profit turnaround claims lack verified design-win visibility; TSMC 1.4nm mid-2028 ramp timing assumes no geopolitical/tool delays and sustained hyperscaler demand.
